title: Move scheduler_providers.dart's projection/plan-building business logic into the domain layer
why: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan are ~200-line pure-ish business-logic functions (amnesty cutoffs, program-vs-self-paced branching, prior-completion filtering) that belong in domain/services or domain/projection — both of which already exist as sibling directories in this exact feature for exactly this purpose. Worse, both functions take `Ref ref` directly as a parameter even though the SAME function signatures already inject `getScopedContent` and `programRepository` as plain callbacks specifically so the logic can be tested without booting Riverpod — the `ref` param undermines that seam (it's used only for one call, `curriculumLabelTextFromRef(ref, curriculum: ...)`, which could equally be injected as a callback like the others). This is why this file is 1381 lines and why testing this logic requires a real ProviderContainer instead of plain unit tests.
recommendation: Extract _buildProjectionTasks/_buildFreshPlan/_applyProgramCalendarOverrides/programCalendarSchedule to a domain/projection or domain/services class; replace the `Ref ref` parameter with a plain `String Function(CurriculumId) trackLabelFor` callback matching the existing DI pattern used for getScopedContent/programRepository.
acceptance_criteria: _buildProjectionTasks and _buildFreshPlan (or their relocated equivalents) take no Ref parameter.
A new domain-layer unit test exercises the amnesty-cutoff and program-vs-self-paced branching logic without a ProviderContainer.
scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart continues to pass unmodified in behavior.

corrections: The evidence array only quotes _buildProjectionTasks's signature (lines 496-497); the parallel claim about _buildFreshPlan (line 940 'required Ref ref,' / line 977 sole use) is asserted in prose but not independently cited — I verified it separately and it holds. Also '~200-line' undersells _buildProjectionTasks, which actually spans ~440 lines (496-935).
